summary: Iteration 2: Validated all NEW security fixes (Option B) and NEW features (Option C). 28/28 backend pytests pass (15 regression + 13 new). All new frontend pages (Preferences, Subscriptions, Orders w/ QR+Review, Vendor VerifyPickup) work end-to-end against live API.

minor.issue: Returns 500 (not 404) when called with a non-existent ObjectId (e.g., bson.errors.InvalidId not caught). Same pattern likely applies to other endpoints accepting raw order/vendor ids.

Brute-force record uses both ip:email and email-only identifiers but never clears the email-only lockout after lockout_minutes; lockout will be cleared only when next attempt arrives after window. Acceptable but worth noting.
Allows reviewing 'ready' orders too (status check is ['completed','ready']). Spec says completed only; tighten to status=='completed' only.

integration_issues.issue: When QR is malformed/order not found, the frontend shows generic 'Verification failed' (the backend actually returned 500 due to invalid ObjectId). Functionally fine for happy path but error surface masks the 500.

issues: Configure-Your-Subscription panel renders ONLY after selecting a plan; not discoverable on first load (minor UX).

action_items: Wrap ObjectId(...) parsing in a helper that returns 404/400 instead of raising 500 (verify-pickup, get_vendor, update_menu_item, payments/checkout, reviews, PATCH /orders/{id}).
Tighten review eligibility to status == 'completed' only (not 'ready').
Optional: also cap brute-force lockout cleanup on the email-only key to align TTL with ip:email key.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew to ~965 lines mixing auth, orders, payments, preferences, subs, reviews - split into FastAPI routers (auth_router, order_router, etc.) and move helpers to /app/backend/utils.
verify_pickup, get_vendor, update_menu_item, payments routes call ObjectId(id) without try/except -> uncaught bson InvalidId -> HTTP 500 on garbage inputs.
PATCH /api/orders/{id} accepts status as query param (FastAPI default for non-model arg); document this in the API contract or move to JSON body to match REST conventions.
Brute force keys never expire from MongoDB; consider TTL index on locked_until or a periodic cleanup.
Reviews logic permits 'ready' status which contradicts spec 'only completed orders can be reviewed'.
seed_demo_data still writes /app/memory/test_credentials.md on every startup - side effect, gate behind env flag.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on new pages (Preferences toggle+save, Subscriptions plan+subscribe, Orders QR+Review form, Vendor VerifyPickup)

test_credentials: Used /app/memory/test_credentials.md unchanged. Brute-force test created TEST_brute_<ts>@cravitoo.com and locked it for 15 min (cleared automatically).
seed_data_creation: No seed data added. Test artifacts: subscriptions for employee@techcorp.com, preferences row for employee, one TEST_great! review on completed order, multiple TEST orders. Safe to leave.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Two backend test files exist: backend_test.py (15 regression) and test_new_features.py (13 new). Run both via: pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v. Frontend new pages all rendered; data-testids in place. Known minor issues: (a) verify-pickup returns 500 on invalid ObjectId, (b) reviews allow 'ready' status orders. Stripe checkout flow only tested to URL creation, not full payment confirmation. No retest needed for Option B/C scope.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A - all targeted features pass. Minor 500-on-invalid-ObjectId is a defensive-coding gap (no try/except around ObjectId()), not a feature bug.
